CARES Architecture Decision Package — Gap Analysis Round 2

Status: Documentation-only architecture review. All SQL and protocol examples are illustrative proposals, not production migrations or implemented controls.

Status labels

  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT — mandatory CARES decision preserved by this review.
  • EXISTING PROPOSAL — already described in CARES architecture documents; not an approved implementation.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION — additional design recommendation for owner and engineering review.
  • OWNER DECISION REQUIRED — product, commercial, privacy, legal, or security decision not made here.
  • IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED — supported by actual implementation and relevant tests.
  • NOT IMPLEMENTED — no working implementation exists.
  • NOT TESTED — no relevant PostgreSQL/integration/security test evidence exists.

1. Executive summary

1.1 Conclusions

  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: CARES uses Python, PostgreSQL as its primary relational database, external SaaS providers for MELIRA, and no local GPU requirement. Core security functionality must work without AI.
  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: One unique monitored device is exactly one licensed asset. Multiple connectors reporting that device do not create multiple billable assets. Connectors/data sources are not billable assets.
  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: The original ten-phase CARES roadmap in CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md remains the baseline and is not changed by this review.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Correct the source-identifier FK by making the identifier-record key include tenant, data source, and stable source-device key, then reference that exact composite key from each rotation item.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Use durable per-attempt rotation history, expiring leases, fenced worker tokens, bounded exponential retries, and explicit terminal run semantics. A failed run is immutable/terminal; recoverable outages pause and resume the same run; an exhausted/permanent item can be retried only through an auditable authorized action or a linked new run.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Treat cross-source identity as a distinct, evidence-based resolution problem. Automatically attach a connector only through a currently valid, authenticated, unique authoritative claim. Weak attributes and numeric confidence scores may rank candidates but never authorize an automatic merge or asset attachment.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Use transaction-scoped, signed tenant context verified by a narrowly privileged database function before RLS policies expose tenant rows. A plain caller-set app.tenant_id is not a trusted security boundary.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Model merge/split as durable, idempotent operations with normalized source-binding assignment history, immutable event attribution, lineage links, licensing ledger entries, and a transactional outbox. Post-commit reversal is a compensating operation, not deletion or rewriting.

1.2 Implementation status and readiness

  • NOT IMPLEMENTED: PostgreSQL, RLS, trusted tenant context, cross-source identity resolution, source-identifier encryption/KMS, fingerprint rotation, asset licensing persistence, operation lineage, and merge/split workflows.
  • NOT TESTED: The illustrative DDL and all race, retry, isolation, recovery, merge/split, and restore behaviors described here.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: The design is substantially more specific, but not ready for production migration creation. It is suitable for formal PostgreSQL/security schema review after owner decisions on identity evidence and lifecycle/billing policies. A few platform choices (notably context-token verification implementation and policy-to-key-state enforcement) must be settled in that review.

2. Findings from the previous gap analysis

The prior document, ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md, established useful proposals: stable internal source-device keys, versioned fingerprint aliases, recoverable identifiers for approved sources, persistent rotation work items, a separate pending identity case, lifecycle/billing separation, and compensating merge/split history.

Round 2 confirms and refines those proposals:

Prior finding/design Round 2 review
Old HMAC digests cannot be transformed to new HMACs Confirmed. Re-fingerprint from retained/decrypted original identifier or wait for authenticated re-observation; never re-HMAC the digest.
source_device_key_id should remain stable through key rotation Confirmed. It is a CARES-generated internal UUID scoped to one tenant/data-source binding, not a source-provided ID or credential.
Alias identity includes key identity/version Confirmed. The alias key includes fingerprint_key_id, which must immutably determine purpose, algorithm, version, normalization, and tenant scope.
A cursor such as last_binding_id is not a correctness boundary Confirmed. Use durable work items, registration dual-write after cutover, and final anti-join verification.
Pending identity should be separate from a canonical asset Confirmed and made concrete: a pending binding may exist with a stable source key but has no asset_id; it cannot be billable or enter normal asset analysis.
Merge/split needs lineage and compensation Confirmed and expanded into operation, binding-assignment, event-lineage, license-ledger, and outbox records.
Tenant RLS/context needs further design Expanded below. Plain transaction-local tenant ID supplied by the application is not sufficient against arbitrary SQL executed under the shared runtime role.
Original ten-phase roadmap is the approved baseline Preserved unchanged. This document proposes no phase reorder or reassignment.

Critical DDL defect identified

The previous illustrative DDL used:

FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, old_identifier_record_id)
    REFERENCES source_device_identifier_secret
        (tenant_id, identifier_record_id)

This guarantees only that the identifier record belongs to the same tenant. It does not guarantee it belongs to the same data_source_id and source_device_key_id recorded on the rotation item. A valid row from another connector or binding in the same tenant could be attached to the item.

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Define the identifier secret's primary key as (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id, identifier_record_id) and make the rotation item reference exactly those four columns. This avoids an additional redundant unique constraint and makes the intended relationship declarative.

3. Workstream A — PostgreSQL relational integrity

3.1 Relationship and enforcement review

Relationship Required DB constraint Additional protocol/trigger requirement
Data source → tenant (tenant_id, data_source_id) primary key; tenant FK Tenant enrollment/authorization is application identity logic
Asset → tenant (tenant_id, asset_id) primary key; tenant FK Asset state transitions and identity verification
Source binding → data source Composite FK (tenant_id, data_source_id) Only authorized connector credential can write its binding
Source binding → asset Nullable composite FK (tenant_id, asset_id) State/assignment transition must be atomic and authorized; pending bindings have no asset
Identifier secret → binding Composite FK (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id) AEAD AAD correctness and secret-retention policy are outside ordinary FK enforcement
Rotation alias → binding Composite FK including tenant and data source Alias may only be made resolvable according to key/policy state
Rotation alias → fingerprint key Composite FK (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id) Key purpose/state/tenant policy agreement needs a transaction protocol or trigger
Rotation run → old/new keys Composite tenant/key FKs Correct key role, status, and active/overlap transition require policy-row lock/procedure
Rotation item → run Composite FK (tenant_id, run_id) Run/item state transition and worker fencing
Rotation item → binding Composite FK (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id) Whether the binding remains eligible is rechecked under lock
Rotation item → identifier record Composite FK of tenant, data source, source-device key, and identifier-record ID Prevents same-tenant cross-source/cross-binding reference
Identity claim → asset Composite FK (tenant_id, asset_id) Evidence quality and authority classification are application-reviewed
Identity claim provenance → binding Composite FK with MATCH SIMPLE plus a check that nullable source columns are both present or both absent A binding cannot be reassigned to an asset solely from claim text
Pending case → binding Composite tenant/source/binding FK Resolution must update case, binding, asset, quota, audit in one transaction
Operation → assets/bindings/events Tenant-inclusive FKs on normalized operation-item tables Authorization, evidence review, transition semantics, and external effects
Outbox → operation Composite tenant/operation FK Consumer idempotency and external API semantics

Constraints versus protocols:

  • Ordinary PostgreSQL constraints can enforce: row-level tenant/source/key relationships; exact alias uniqueness; one binding row's current single asset assignment; one current protected identifier per binding; stable item idempotency keys; one active/overlap key-state row per tenant/purpose; event/operation/outbox references.
  • Triggers or controlled stored procedures may be needed for: key registry state matching tenant_fingerprint_policy; legal asset lifecycle transitions; forbidding direct binding reassignment without a committed operation item; append-only ledger/audit protection; ensuring a claim's fingerprint key has the expected purpose; ensuring resolution changes pending case and binding state coherently.
  • Transaction protocols remain essential for: quota serialization, conflict resolution, identity authority, rotation leases, same-device assertions across sources, authorization, event-lineage decisions, and outbox delivery.
  • A CHECK constraint cannot safely assert arbitrary cross-table state. Do not duplicate state columns merely to simulate a cross-table CHECK unless a trigger/procedure and consistency tests are specified.

3.2 Illustrative DDL — tenant, assets, sources, fingerprints

The following is a coherent conceptual subset, not a migration. It omits production grants, full audit schema, event partitions, policies, and key-management implementation details.

CREATE TABLE tenant (
    tenant_id uuid PRIMARY KEY
);

CREATE TABLE data_source (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant (tenant_id),
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_kind text NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('active', 'disabled', 'removed')),
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id)
);

CREATE TABLE asset (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant (tenant_id),
    asset_id uuid NOT NULL,
    lifecycle_state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        lifecycle_state IN ('active', 'inactive', 'deactivated', 'reserved',
                            'removed', 'merged')
    ),
    merged_into_asset_id uuid,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, merged_into_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id),
    CHECK (merged_into_asset_id IS NULL OR merged_into_asset_id <> asset_id),
    CHECK (
        (lifecycle_state = 'merged' AND merged_into_asset_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR
        (lifecycle_state <> 'merged' AND merged_into_asset_id IS NULL)
    )
);

CREATE TABLE fingerprint_key (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant (tenant_id),
    fingerprint_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    purpose text NOT NULL CHECK (
        purpose IN ('source-device-identity', 'cross-source-identity')
    ),
    key_version bigint NOT NULL CHECK (key_version > 0),
    algorithm text NOT NULL CHECK (algorithm = 'HMAC-SHA-256'),
    normalization_version text NOT NULL,
    scope text NOT NULL CHECK (scope = 'tenant'),
    secret_ref text NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('staged', 'active', 'overlap', 'retiring', 'retired', 'revoked')
    ),
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, purpose, key_version)
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX fingerprint_key_one_active_per_purpose
    ON fingerprint_key (tenant_id, purpose)
    WHERE state = 'active';

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX fingerprint_key_one_overlap_per_purpose
    ON fingerprint_key (tenant_id, purpose)
    WHERE state = 'overlap';

CREATE TABLE tenant_fingerprint_policy (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant (tenant_id),
    purpose text NOT NULL CHECK (purpose = 'source-device-identity'),
    active_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    overlap_key_id uuid,
    generation bigint NOT NULL CHECK (generation > 0),
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, purpose),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, active_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_key (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, overlap_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_key (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    CHECK (overlap_key_id IS NULL OR overlap_key_id <> active_key_id)
);

CREATE TABLE source_device_binding (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    asset_id uuid,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('pending', 'active', 'inactive', 'conflict', 'removed')
    ),
    first_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    last_seen_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id)
        REFERENCES data_source (tenant_id, data_source_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'pending' AND asset_id IS NULL)
        OR (state IN ('active', 'inactive') AND asset_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR state IN ('conflict', 'removed')
    )
);

CREATE TABLE source_device_identifier_secret (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    identifier_record_id uuid NOT NULL,
    identifier_type text NOT NULL,
    normalization_version text NOT NULL,
    encryption_algorithm text NOT NULL
        CHECK (encryption_algorithm IN ('AES-256-GCM', 'CHACHA20-POLY1305')),
    encryption_key_ref text NOT NULL,
    nonce bytea NOT NULL,
    ciphertext bytea NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('current', 'superseded', 'deleted')),
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    retired_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (
        tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id, identifier_record_id
    ),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES source_device_binding
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'superseded' AND retired_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR state IN ('current', 'deleted')
    )
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX source_device_one_current_secret
    ON source_device_identifier_secret
        (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
    WHERE state = 'current';

CREATE TABLE source_device_fingerprint_alias (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    fingerprint_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    fingerprint_digest bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(fingerprint_digest) = 32),
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('active', 'overlap', 'deprecated', 'retired')
    ),
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    retired_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (
        tenant_id, data_source_id, fingerprint_key_id, fingerprint_digest
    ),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES source_device_binding
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_key (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    CHECK (
        (state IN ('deprecated', 'retired') AND retired_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR state IN ('active', 'overlap')
    )
);

There is deliberately no uniqueness constraint on data_source_id alone: one connector may report many devices. A source-device key is unique only in its tenant/data-source namespace. One binding row has one nullable current asset_id; pending bindings have none.

3.3 Illustrative DDL — rotation runs, items, and exact identifier reference

CREATE TABLE fingerprint_rotation_run (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    run_id uuid NOT NULL,
    purpose text NOT NULL CHECK (purpose = 'source-device-identity'),
    old_key_id uuid,
    new_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('preparing', 'running', 'paused', 'needs_review',
                  'verifying', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled')
    ),
    max_automatic_attempts integer NOT NULL CHECK (max_automatic_attempts > 0),
    backoff_base_ms integer NOT NULL CHECK (backoff_base_ms > 0),
    backoff_cap_ms integer NOT NULL CHECK (backoff_cap_ms >= backoff_base_ms),
    retry_policy_version text NOT NULL,
    authorized_by text NOT NULL,
    authorization_ref text NOT NULL,
    parent_run_id uuid,
    started_at timestamptz,
    completed_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, run_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, new_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, old_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_key (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, new_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_key (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, parent_run_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_rotation_run (tenant_id, run_id)
);

CREATE TABLE fingerprint_rotation_item (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    run_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    old_identifier_record_id uuid,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('queued', 'leased', 'retry_wait', 'awaiting_observation',
                  'conflict', 'permanent_failure', 'complete', 'skipped')
    ),
    attempt_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempt_count >= 0),
    next_attempt_at timestamptz,
    lease_owner text,
    lease_token uuid,
    lease_until timestamptz,
    last_error_class text,
    last_error_code text,
    updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, run_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, run_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_rotation_run (tenant_id, run_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES source_device_binding
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (
        tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id, old_identifier_record_id
    )
        REFERENCES source_device_identifier_secret
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id, identifier_record_id),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'leased' AND lease_owner IS NOT NULL
                          AND lease_token IS NOT NULL AND lease_until IS NOT NULL)
        OR
        (state <> 'leased' AND lease_owner IS NULL
                           AND lease_token IS NULL AND lease_until IS NULL)
    ),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'retry_wait' AND next_attempt_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR state <> 'retry_wait'
    )
);

CREATE INDEX fingerprint_rotation_ready_items
    ON fingerprint_rotation_item (tenant_id, run_id, next_attempt_at)
    WHERE state IN ('queued', 'retry_wait');

CREATE INDEX fingerprint_rotation_expired_leases
    ON fingerprint_rotation_item (tenant_id, run_id, lease_until)
    WHERE state = 'leased';

CREATE TABLE fingerprint_rotation_attempt (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    run_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    attempt_number integer NOT NULL CHECK (attempt_number > 0),
    attempt_kind text NOT NULL CHECK (
        attempt_kind IN ('automatic', 'manual_retry', 'lease_reclaim')
    ),
    worker_id text,
    lease_token uuid,
    started_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    completed_at timestamptz,
    outcome text CHECK (
        outcome IN ('success', 'retryable_failure', 'permanent_failure',
                    'conflict', 'abandoned_lease', 'cancelled')
    ),
    error_class text,
    error_code text,
    authorization_ref text,
    PRIMARY KEY (
        tenant_id, run_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id, attempt_number
    ),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, run_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_rotation_item
            (tenant_id, run_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    CHECK (
        (attempt_kind = 'manual_retry' AND authorization_ref IS NOT NULL)
        OR attempt_kind <> 'manual_retry'
    ),
    CHECK (
        (completed_at IS NULL AND outcome IS NULL)
        OR (completed_at IS NOT NULL AND outcome IS NOT NULL)
    )
);

The nullable old_identifier_record_id causes the composite FK to be skipped under MATCH SIMPLE when that identifier is absent. When it is present, all four values must match the same secret row. The key is the table's primary key, so no extra, logically redundant UNIQUE constraint is required.

source_device_key_id is a CARES-generated random UUID, stable for the source-local binding and not supplied to or trusted from an API request. It is not a canonical cross-source device ID. A binding can have multiple aliases across fingerprint keys and multiple encrypted identifier records over time. An authenticated identifier change updates the secret history and can add an alias to the same binding without changing the canonical asset or quota.

3.4 Other constraints and invariants not covered by ordinary FKs

  • Policy/key-state agreement: tenant_fingerprint_policy.active_key_id must reference the one key in active state and overlap_key_id the one in overlap state with matching purpose. An ordinary FK cannot enforce referenced-row values. Use a single locked transition procedure or a carefully reviewed deferred constraint trigger; restrict direct key/policy writes.
  • Rotation item alias consistency: an item marked complete must have the new alias for the same binding. This is a cross-table invariant; set item state and alias atomically in one transaction and verify with anti-join queries. A trigger is optional but must not be a substitute for final run verification.
  • Binding identity resolution: the illustrative CHECK requires pending bindings to have no asset and active/inactive bindings to have one; conflict/removed may retain or lack an asset for historical/quarantine cases. The final schema must tighten those states to the approved lifecycle. Updating an assigned binding to another asset must require a resolution/merge/split operation. Enforce through stored procedures/trigger plus restrictive grants or an application transaction protocol, not an unrestricted update.
  • Key purpose: a source alias must reference a source-device key; a cross-source claim alias must reference a cross-source key. A trigger/procedure or separate key tables are needed because the alias FK cannot enforce a value in the referenced row.
  • Single current secret per binding: the partial unique index enforces this. It does not ensure the stored ciphertext was encrypted with specified AAD or that the referenced KMS key is live.
  • No duplicate exact exclusive identity claim: a partial unique index on active exclusive claim aliases (below) enforces at most one current target per exact namespace/key-version/digest. Nonexclusive observations may be associated with multiple assets. This cannot prove that the claimed physical-device identity is true.
  • Lifecycle state transitions and nonnegative quota: use a locked transactional licensing procedure and check constraints for simple local facts. A cross-row quota calculation is not a CHECK constraint.
  • Append-only audit/ledger: database grants and append-only service interfaces are required; a table owner or superuser can still change rows. Add tamper-evident external audit/export if the threat model requires it.
  • No redundant uniqueness: do not repeat a primary-key column set as a unique constraint. Add an alternate unique key only when another table must reference that exact composite, or when it represents a distinct invariant.

4. Workstream B — Rotation retry and recovery semantics

4.1 Error classes and retry policy

All values below are NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION, not deployed settings.

Failure class Examples Item action Run action
Transient database Serialization failure, deadlock, transient connection loss, bounded lock timeout Retry with backoff; same operation/idempotency keys Continue unless outage is broad
Transient KMS/service Timeout, throttling, temporary 5xx, network outage Persist attempt; retry_wait Pause run if health check/circuit breaker indicates shared outage
Key unavailable/revoked HMAC key disabled or authorization removed Do not guess or transform digest; use encrypted-ID route only if separately authorized Pause and alert; security/key owner classifies and authorizes recovery
Stale observation Identifier changed between preparation and apply Discard calculated digest; reread current secret/observation Continue after requeue
Identity conflict New digest already owned by a different binding Do not overwrite or merge; mark conflict needs_review; unrelated items may continue only if policy permits
Permanent data/crypto AEAD authentication failure, malformed normalized identity, impossible digest length Mark permanent_failure; preserve evidence and sanitized code needs_review or failed, depending on blast radius
Authorization/security violation Invalid tenant context, unauthorized key use, tampered lease token Do not retry as ordinary work; emit security audit/alert Fail or pause entire run; require security review
Capacity/operational shutdown Maintenance window, worker deployment Keep queued or pause Resume same run after health checks

Proposed automatic retry: at most 8 attempts per item, exponential backoff min(base × 2^(attempt-1), cap) with full jitter, with a recommended 1-second base and 15-minute cap. Honor KMS/server Retry-After when bounded by the policy. A shared KMS outage should trip a circuit breaker and pause rather than rapidly exhaust every item's attempts. These values require operational validation.

4.2 Rotation-item state transition table

Current state Event/condition Next state Requirements
queued Worker claims item leased Atomic claim, random lease token, owner, expiry, increment attempt and append attempt record
retry_wait next_attempt_at reached and run is running leased Claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; issue a new lease token
leased Alias inserted and verified for same binding complete Alias, item, attempt outcome, and audit commit in one transaction
leased Retryable transient failure below limit retry_wait Record sanitized class/code and next_attempt_at; clear lease
leased Retry limit reached permanent_failure Preserve final attempt and diagnostics; require authorized retry/new run
leased Worker lease expires queued or retry_wait Reclaimer locks item, records abandoned lease, clears old token; prior worker is fenced
leased Conflicting alias/identity conflict Preserve both mappings; no reassign/merge
leased Source offline, no recoverable identifier awaiting_observation No repeated polling retries; await authenticated observation or approved disposition
awaiting_observation Source re-observed and identity proof is valid queued Record evidence and operator/system action; compute new alias from fresh source value
conflict Human resolves conflict with evidence queued Authorized resolution event; do not erase conflict history
permanent_failure Manual retry approved after cause fixed queued in a new retry generation or linked run New auditable authorization/attempt; no silent counter reset
Nonterminal Run cancelled skipped or retained terminal disposition Stop claims; keep aliases and audit; no broad deletion

An item attempt history is append-only: attempt number/generation, worker identity, lease token hash/reference, start/end time, error class/code, and outcome. The current item state is a projection; prior failures are not overwritten.

4.3 Rotation-run state transition table

Current run state Event/condition Next state Same run may resume?
preparing Key staged, policy transition committed running Yes
preparing Key/config preflight fails before cutover failed or cancelled No; create linked run after correction
running Explicit maintenance pause or shared transient dependency outage paused Yes, after health checks
paused KMS/database healthy and authorized resume running Yes
running Conflict, exhausted item, or unresolved source requires decision needs_review Yes, after reviewed item disposition
needs_review Authorized resolution/retry recorded running Yes, preserving item/attempt history
running No eligible work remains; final scan begins verifying Yes; recoverable verification issue returns to paused or needs_review
verifying Anti-join, alias consistency and run criteria pass completed No
verifying Recoverable service outage paused Yes
Any nonterminal Integrity/security failure makes continuation unsafe failed No; failed run is terminal
Any nonterminal Authorized cancellation cancelled No; create linked run if work is later required

completed, failed, and cancelled runs are immutable terminal records. A transient outage is not a reason to mark a run failed. A failed/cancelled run is never reset in place; create a new run with parent_run_id, preserve its outcomes, and explicitly select eligible bindings for the new run.

4.4 Lease fencing, retry, and crash recovery

  1. A worker claims one bounded batch in a short transaction with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; it stores a random lease_token, worker identity, and lease_until.
  2. KMS calls and digest preparation occur outside database row locks. The worker retains the identifier-record key/version it read.
  3. Before applying results, the worker locks the policy row, any relevant asset, the binding, then run/item in the globally documented order. It verifies run state, token equality, and lease_until > clock_timestamp(). A stale worker cannot commit after its lease expires or is reclaimed.
  4. The apply transaction inserts the alias, item outcome, attempt result, and audit event atomically. A conflict is persisted as a conflict; no alias reassignment or asset creation occurs.
  5. A reclaimer locks expired items, appends an abandoned_lease attempt outcome, clears the old token, and returns eligible work to queued/retry_wait. If another worker has already obtained a new token, the stale worker's compare-and-set fails.
  6. If commit succeeds but the client times out, the caller reads the unique item/alias/attempt keys. A committed result is returned; otherwise it retries. It does not infer failure from the timeout.
  7. An unexpected KMS outage pauses the run after bounded health checks; work resumes under the same run once keys, grants, and service health are confirmed.
  8. A permanently failed item can return to work only through an authorized, recorded retry generation after remediation. If the run itself is terminal failed, retry in a new linked run.
  9. Cancellation stops new claims. In-flight transactions either commit their atomic unit before cancellation wins the run lock, or observe the terminal state and roll back. New aliases are retained until a separate reviewed retirement procedure.

4.5 Crash/retry scenarios

Scenario Expected result
Crash before claim commit No lease is visible; another worker claims normally
Crash after claim commit, before KMS Lease expires; reclaimer fences old worker and requeues
Crash after KMS, before apply Lease expires; retry recomputes or reuses transient in-memory result only if still valid; no DB identity change occurred
Crash after alias insert but before item update Impossible as a partial commit if both are in one transaction; transaction rolls back or both commit
Commit succeeds, response lost Read back idempotent item and alias state; return committed result
Two workers process same item Row lock/SKIP LOCKED, lease token, expiry check, and alias PK prevent duplicate application
Identifier rotates during KMS call Apply sees different current identifier record/version; old calculation discarded
KMS outage lasts beyond retry cap Pause run globally; do not permanently fail every item
Old HMAC key revoked Re-fingerprint from encrypted identifier if authorized; otherwise wait for proven re-observation or require reviewed exception
Alias collision discovered Item enters conflict/needs-review; never merge bindings or assets automatically
Manual resolution Append resolution evidence and actor; retry under same nonterminal run or create linked run if prior run is terminal

5. Workstream C — Cross-source asset identity resolution

5.1 Three identities, not one

  1. Source-local identity: Identifier as emitted by one source/connector, namespaced by authenticated (tenant_id, data_source_id) and the source's identifier type/normalization. A firewall's endpoint IP and a scanner's target row ID are source-local observations, not necessarily device identity.
  2. Source-device binding: Stable CARES UUID source_device_key_id for one source-local identity within one connector instance. It binds that source's representation to zero or one canonical CARES asset. One connector has many bindings.
  3. Canonical CARES asset identity: Immutable tenant-scoped asset_id representing one verified physical or logical monitored device. Many source-device bindings from different connectors can attach to one asset. Asset ID is never derived from an IP, hostname, HMAC, or connector ID.

The approved source-binding namespace remains (tenant_id, data_source_id, protected_source_device_key_fingerprint); the fingerprint alias is versioned, and key rotation does not change source_device_key_id or asset_id.

5.2 Evidence classes and decision rules

Evidence class Examples Permitted action
Existing authenticated binding Exact alias from the same authorized source namespace Use its current asset if binding is active; no new licensed usage
Verified authoritative claim Fresh authenticated CARES enrollment credential; provider resource identity scoped by provider/account/region and verified as unique; signed inventory mapping with trusted issuer and explicit physical/logical semantics May attach a new source binding to the single asset that owns the exact active claim, if connector-specific policy approves that claim as authoritative
Strong but non-authoritative evidence Correlated agent/CMDB mapping, scanner-to-CMDB relationship, corroborating hardware data with provenance Candidate suggestion; human confirmation or a separately approved source-specific deterministic rule is required
Weak or mutable attribute IP, hostname, MAC, display name, operating-system text, unverified serial, confidence score Candidate ranking only; never automatic merge or binding
Conflicting evidence Same exclusive claim on different assets, duplicate agent credential, inconsistent provider IDs, incompatible hardware claims Mandatory quarantine and human/security review

No aggregate confidence score, however high, overrides the evidence rule. A score may order a review queue; it is not an authorization to merge or attach.

An “attach” is a source-binding assignment to a canonical asset; it is not permission to merge two existing canonical assets. If an authoritative claim points to multiple existing assets, stop and resolve the conflict before any merge.

5.3 Registration decision procedure

authenticate source credential
resolve tenant_id and data_source_id from trusted server-side credential mapping
normalize source-local identity according to source-specific version
resolve existing (tenant, data_source, fingerprint alias) binding

if binding exists and is active:
    use its one assigned canonical asset
    add no licensed usage
else:
    collect verified identity claims and provenance
    if exactly one current authoritative claim maps to one active asset:
        lock tenant licensing state and target asset
        recheck claim uniqueness and source binding
        attach binding to that asset atomically; add no usage
    else if any plausible existing-asset candidate or identity conflict exists:
        create/retain a pending identity case; no canonical asset, no billable count
        quarantine or reject normal asset-attributed data
    else if source policy proves a new unique device identity:
        atomically create one canonical asset and binding; increment usage once
    else:
        create pending identity case; do not guess and do not bill

An operator-confirmed mapping follows the same transaction, records actor/reason/evidence, and has an idempotency key. A support operator cannot make a cross-tenant mapping without a valid, scoped JIT grant.

**Important limit:** If two connectors emit unrelated opaque IDs and neither shares a trusted inventory/enrollment claim nor is manually mapped, no algorithm can prove whether they represent one device or two. The safe behavior is to keep the uncertain binding pending, not create a second billable asset and not merge by guess. To meet the one-device/one-asset requirement operationally, every source that can originate licensed assets needs an approved cross-source identity path (for example, CARES enrollment or a validated inventory mapping); passive/observation-only connectors must not create billable assets on their own. This is an identity-capability/product decision, not a property a relational constraint can solve.

5.4 Cross-source scenarios

Scenario Safe resolution
Linux Agent and firewall report the same server The agent's authenticated enrollment can identify its asset. A firewall flow/IP observation is not the agent identity. Attach firewall source only if it supplies a verified claim or an authorized inventory/operator mapping; otherwise pending. Do not create a second billable asset solely from firewall IP/hostname.
Multiple vulnerability scanners report the same device Scanner target IDs remain connector-local. Map each target to an asset through a verified common claim, trusted inventory integration, or reviewed mapping. Repeated scan records do not each create an asset. Ambiguous targets remain pending/unattributed.
IP address changes Preserve device identity through stable authenticated claims/binding. Record IP as time-bounded observation; do not create a new asset or rewrite the canonical ID.
Hostname changes Preserve stable identity; record hostname history as mutable observation. Hostname change does not create, merge, or split assets.
IP is reused by another host Use address validity times and source provenance only as evidence. Never attach the new observation to the previous IP owner solely by address; quarantine if no stronger claim exists.
Cloned virtual machines Treat cloned agent keys/machine IDs as a conflict signal, not proof of sameness. Require unique enrollment credential rotation/re-enrollment or verified cloud resource identity. A cloud instance identity must include its provider/account/region scope and lifecycle semantics.
Device replacement using same IP/hostname Replacement is a new physical/logical device unless an authorized replacement workflow explicitly preserves a logical asset identity. Decommission old identity separately; mutable endpoint attributes do not merge.
Conflicting hardware IDs Conflicting serial/MAC/agent/provider claims create a conflict case with evidence/provenance. Human/security review is mandatory; no “majority vote” or confidence threshold auto-merges.
One connector reports many devices Each normalized source-local device key gets its own binding/alias. No uniqueness on data_source_id alone.
One device appears through many connectors Each connector has a distinct source binding. Verified cross-source claims map those bindings to the same asset; attaching later sources adds zero licenses.

5.5 Illustrative identity-claim and pending-case DDL

This is a conceptual extension to Section 3, not complete product schema. It defines exact claim aliases with versioned key identity and ensures an active exclusive fingerprint maps to one claim in its tenant/namespace.

CREATE TABLE asset_identity_claim (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    claim_id uuid NOT NULL,
    asset_id uuid NOT NULL,
    identifier_namespace text NOT NULL,
    authority_class text NOT NULL CHECK (
        authority_class IN ('authoritative', 'corroborating', 'weak', 'manual_verified')
    ),
    exclusivity text NOT NULL CHECK (exclusivity IN ('exclusive', 'nonexclusive')),
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('active', 'superseded', 'conflict', 'revoked')),
    issuer text NOT NULL,
    provenance_ref text NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid,
    source_device_key_id uuid,
    normalization_version text NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    revoked_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, claim_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, claim_id, identifier_namespace, exclusivity),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES source_device_binding
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        MATCH SIMPLE,
    CHECK ((data_source_id IS NULL) = (source_device_key_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'revoked' AND revoked_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR state <> 'revoked'
    )
);

CREATE TABLE asset_identity_claim_alias (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    identifier_namespace text NOT NULL,
    claim_id uuid NOT NULL,
    fingerprint_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    claim_digest bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(claim_digest) = 32),
    exclusivity text NOT NULL CHECK (exclusivity IN ('exclusive', 'nonexclusive')),
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('active', 'retired')),
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    retired_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, claim_id, fingerprint_key_id, claim_digest),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, claim_id, identifier_namespace, exclusivity)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_claim
            (tenant_id, claim_id, identifier_namespace, exclusivity),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id)
        REFERENCES fingerprint_key (tenant_id, fingerprint_key_id),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'retired' AND retired_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR state = 'active'
    )
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_active_exclusive_claim_alias
    ON asset_identity_claim_alias
        (tenant_id, identifier_namespace, fingerprint_key_id, claim_digest)
    WHERE state = 'active' AND exclusivity = 'exclusive';

CREATE TABLE identity_resolution_case (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    case_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('open', 'reviewing', 'resolved_existing', 'resolved_new',
                  'rejected', 'expired')
    ),
    reason_code text NOT NULL,
    opened_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    closed_at timestamptz,
    resolved_asset_id uuid,
    idempotency_key text NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, case_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES source_device_binding
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, resolved_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id),
    CHECK (
        (state IN ('resolved_existing', 'resolved_new') AND
         closed_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_asset_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR
        (state IN ('rejected', 'expired') AND
         closed_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_asset_id IS NULL)
        OR
        (state IN ('open', 'reviewing') AND
         closed_at IS NULL AND resolved_asset_id IS NULL)
    )
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_open_identity_case_per_binding
    ON identity_resolution_case
        (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
    WHERE state IN ('open', 'reviewing');

asset_identity_claim uses MATCH SIMPLE plus a local check that the nullable provenance columns are both present or both absent. MATCH FULL across a composite key that includes the required non-null tenant_id would incorrectly reject the absent-source case.

asset_identity_claim_alias must also be checked against the parent claim's authority_class and state before auto-resolution. Its exclusivity is constrained to match the parent through the composite FK. Since claim state and authority are cross-row predicates, use a controlled resolution function/transaction or a trigger; do not assume the alias PK proves semantic authority. Claim-key purpose must likewise be checked. If two concurrently active claim-key versions produce aliases for one presented identifier, all matching exclusive aliases must resolve to the same claim/asset; disagreement is an identity conflict, never a tie-break. Nonexclusive observations can legitimately point to multiple claims and are candidate evidence only.

Pending identity cases do not require a canonical asset. Their source_device_binding row is pending with asset_id IS NULL; on resolution, one transaction updates the binding, closes the case, records claim/evidence and audit, and updates licensing only if a new asset is confirmed. Pending quota reservation remains owner policy.

6. Workstream D — PostgreSQL tenant isolation

6.1 Security objective and trust boundaries

EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: Strict tenant isolation is mandatory.

The API request's tenant path/header/body value is a requested scope, not an authenticated tenant identity. It must never be copied directly into database context.

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: For each request, trusted authentication/authorization code:

  1. Validates the OIDC/session/service credential.
  2. Resolves the principal and active membership in a trusted tenant-membership authority.
  3. Confirms the requested tenant is one the principal may access and determines allowed actions.
  4. Obtains a short-lived signed tenant-context assertion from an authorization component that independently enforces membership/scope; ordinary API code cannot sign arbitrary tenant IDs.
  5. Starts a database transaction and passes that assertion to a database verifier before reading or writing tenant rows.

The assertion includes tenant ID, principal/service identity, allowed scope/role, audience, issue/expiry time, request/job ID, nonce, and key/version ID. It is bound to the CARES database audience and short lifetime. The database verifier rejects expired, wrong-audience, malformed, revoked-key, or invalid-signature assertions.

6.2 RLS strategy and transaction-local context

Enable and force RLS on every tenant-owned base table:

ALTER TABLE asset ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE asset FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY asset_tenant_scope
    ON asset
    FOR SELECT
    USING (
        tenant_id = security.current_verified_tenant_id()
        AND security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:read')
    );

CREATE POLICY asset_insert_scope
    ON asset
    FOR INSERT
    WITH CHECK (
        tenant_id = security.current_verified_tenant_id()
        AND security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write')
    );

CREATE POLICY asset_update_scope
    ON asset
    FOR UPDATE
    USING (
        tenant_id = security.current_verified_tenant_id()
        AND security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write')
    )
    WITH CHECK (
        tenant_id = security.current_verified_tenant_id()
        AND security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:write')
    );

CREATE POLICY asset_delete_scope
    ON asset
    FOR DELETE
    USING (
        tenant_id = security.current_verified_tenant_id()
        AND security.current_verified_scope_allows('asset:delete')
    );

Apply equivalent command-specific tenant and scope policies to data sources, bindings, aliases, claims, pending cases, events, alerts, cases, licensing, audit, and outbox rows. A missing/invalid context must resolve to NULL/deny, never to a default tenant.

Important limitation: A plain SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = '<uuid>' is caller-controlled by a shared SQL role. RLS based only on that value prevents many accidental unscoped queries but is not a trusted boundary against arbitrary SQL execution under that role.

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Set a signed context token transaction-locally with a narrowly privileged SECURITY DEFINER function (fixed safe search_path, no dynamic SQL). RLS calls a verifier that validates the token and extracts its tenant/scope; changing a separate tenant-ID GUC cannot change the verified tenant. For the concrete initial proposal, use an HMAC assertion signed by a dedicated authorization service and verified by a narrowly scoped database function (for example, using PostgreSQL pgcrypto). The HMAC key is accessible only to that signer and the verifier's protected owner-only key store/function, never to runtime/worker SQL roles; compromise of the verifier database/key is a trust-boundary compromise and requires key rotation and incident response. The authorization signer independently checks membership and scope and does not sign arbitrary tenant values requested by the API. This is a proposed technology choice, not an installed extension or implemented verifier.

At the start of every tenant transaction:

BEGIN
assert connection has no prior transaction/context
SELECT security.begin_tenant_context(:signed_assertion)
  -> verifies signature, audience, expiry, principal, scope and revocation
perform tenant queries/writes under RLS
COMMIT or ROLLBACK

The begin_tenant_context function stores only transaction-local verified context (set_config(..., true)). RLS obtains tenant and scope only from the verified assertion. No tenant context is accepted as an unverified API parameter. Use parameterized queries; RLS does not make arbitrary SQL safe.

6.3 Runtime, worker, migration, and maintenance roles

Role Permitted design
cares_runtime LOGIN service role; not superuser, not table owner, no BYPASSRLS, no schema CREATE, no membership in owner/migrator roles. Access only required tables/functions. Sensitive asset/identity writes should use reviewed procedures or narrowly granted DML.
cares_worker Separate service identity and minimal queue/outbox privileges. Each tenant job is claimed with a trusted job ID, then receives a signed context limited to that tenant and task. No cross-tenant scan under a broad worker credential.
cares_migrator Separate ephemeral CI/operator identity, not used by application processes. DDL ownership belongs to a NOLOGIN owner role. Migration access is time-bound, approved, logged, and limited to migration windows.
cares_maintenance Separate, narrowly scoped maintenance identity. Partition maintenance, vacuum, backup, and retention duties must not grant general tenant-row reads. Operations needing cross-tenant data use a reviewed job with explicit purpose and audit.
Support/operator No shared table-owner credential. Obtain a JIT grant and tenant/action-scoped signed context; no permanent BYPASSRLS access. Emergency database-owner access is break-glass, separately controlled and audited.

BYPASSRLS and superuser are prohibited for runtime and workers. Table owners are NOLOGIN; FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY makes ordinary owner queries subject to RLS, though a superuser or role with BYPASSRLS can still bypass it. Restrict such roles to isolated deployment/incident procedures; record all uses.

6.4 Connection-pool behavior

  • Never retain tenant context at session scope.
  • Begin and verify context inside the same explicit transaction that performs tenant work.
  • Use transaction-local settings only; commit/rollback clears them automatically.
  • On checkout, reject a connection with an open/failed transaction or nonempty unexpected context.
  • On check-in, roll back any open transaction, clear any session-level custom settings, and verify no context remains before reuse. Quarantine/discard a connection if cleanup is uncertain.
  • Do not multiplex tenants within one transaction. One transaction has one verified tenant scope.
  • Test the actual driver/pool's reset hooks and error paths, including cancellation, timeout, rollback failure, and connection replacement.

6.5 Background jobs and privileged support

Workers must not trust a tenant ID copied from an arbitrary queue payload. A job row is created transactionally with tenant ID and immutable job ID by an authorized API operation. The worker authenticates as a service principal, claims the job, validates the referenced tenant and job scope, and obtains a short-lived signed tenant context bound to (worker identity, tenant, job ID, allowed action). A stale/replayed job context is rejected.

Support access uses a JIT grant containing requester, approver, target tenant, specific action/read-write scope, ticket/reason, issue/expiry time, and revocation status. The authorization service verifies the grant for each context assertion. Policies/functions check the allowed scope; support is not made a member of all tenants and does not receive BYPASSRLS.

6.6 Audit requirements

Record:

  • Context assertion ID/hash, subject/service, tenant, scopes, request/job ID, issue/expiry, result, and authorization policy version.
  • Tenant membership and JIT grant decisions, including denials.
  • Sensitive reads (source identifier decrypt, forensic evidence, cross-source identity claim) and all writes/exports.
  • Migration/maintenance role activation, migration version, operator/CI identity, approval, start/end, outcome.
  • Break-glass access in a separate protected security log, including queries/actions where feasible.

Tenant audit records must be tenant-scoped and append-only to runtime roles. Security administration/audit of cross-tenant access also needs a platform-level protected log; it must not be hidden by the target tenant's RLS policy. No log should include raw source identifiers, key material, or complete context tokens.

6.7 Negative tenant-isolation acceptance scenarios

All tests use the exact production-equivalent runtime/worker roles, not a superuser or table owner:

  1. Tenant A selects/updates/deletes Tenant B rows by guessed UUID: zero rows returned/changed.
  2. Tenant A inserts a row with Tenant B tenant_id: RLS WITH CHECK rejects it.
  3. Tenant A references a Tenant B asset, source, claim, alias, or event: composite FK or RLS rejects it.
  4. Context absent, malformed, expired, wrong audience, invalid signature, revoked signing key, or mismatched scope: transaction fails closed.
  5. Runtime role sets app.tenant_id to B while carrying a valid signed context for A: policy still authorizes only A.
  6. Caller submits B as request tenant but lacks B membership: authorization refuses to mint context; no database transaction with B context starts.
  7. Pool connection is returned after A then borrowed for B, including after exception/cancellation: no A context persists and B context is required.
  8. Worker receives a forged/stale/replayed cross-tenant job ID or task scope: claim/context verification rejects it.
  9. Support grant expired, revoked, wrong tenant, wrong scope, missing approval, or replayed: no access.
  10. Views, partitions, SECURITY DEFINER functions, trigger functions, and maintenance paths do not leak cross-tenant rows or bypass policy.
  11. Runtime and worker roles cannot SET ROLE to owner/migrator, alter policies, disable RLS, or access verifier secrets.
  12. Run concurrent requests for different tenants on pooled connections and verify no cross-request state bleed.

NOT TESTED: No such PostgreSQL role/RLS/context tests currently exist.

7. Workstream E — Merge/split and event lineage

7.1 Operation invariants

EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: Merging two records must not count one device twice; splitting records that represent two verified devices may add one licensed asset, subject to quota policy.

NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION:

  • Canonical asset IDs are immutable and never recycled.
  • Binding assignment is explicit and versioned; one binding has at most one current asset.
  • Original event, alert, incident, and forensic-evidence attribution is immutable.
  • Corrected interpretation is represented by lineage/association rows with operation and evidence references.
  • Every merge/split and compensation is idempotent, tenant-scoped, authorized, and audited.
  • The database transaction commits operation state, binding assignment changes, licensing ledger/counters, lineage rows, audit records, idempotency outcome, and outbox messages together.
  • External integrations are invoked only from the outbox after commit; their results do not retroactively erase committed CARES history.

7.2 Illustrative operation, assignment, lineage, licensing, and outbox DDL

The following references conceptual event_registry, security_alert, incident_case, and forensic_evidence tables with tenant-composite keys. Implementations must align names and partition strategy with the approved event schema. No original evidence row is updated or deleted by these operations.

CREATE TABLE asset_identity_operation (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant (tenant_id),
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_type text NOT NULL CHECK (
        operation_type IN ('merge', 'split', 'compensate_merge', 'compensate_split')
    ),
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('prepared', 'committed', 'failed', 'cancelled')
    ),
    idempotency_key text NOT NULL,
    requested_by text NOT NULL,
    approved_by text,
    reason text NOT NULL,
    evidence_summary_ref text NOT NULL,
    authorization_ref text NOT NULL,
    policy_version text NOT NULL,
    compensates_operation_id uuid,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    committed_at timestamptz,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, operation_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, compensates_operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    CHECK (
        (state = 'committed' AND committed_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR (state <> 'committed' AND committed_at IS NULL)
    )
);

CREATE TABLE asset_identity_operation_asset (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    asset_id uuid NOT NULL,
    asset_role text NOT NULL CHECK (
        asset_role IN ('source', 'survivor', 'created', 'compensation_target')
    ),
    before_state text NOT NULL,
    after_state text NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, operation_id, asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE asset_binding_assignment_history (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    data_source_id uuid NOT NULL,
    source_device_key_id uuid NOT NULL,
    from_asset_id uuid,
    to_asset_id uuid,
    decision text NOT NULL CHECK (
        decision IN ('attach', 'merge_transfer', 'split_transfer', 'compensate')
    ),
    evidence_ref text NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (
        tenant_id, operation_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id
    ),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id)
        REFERENCES source_device_binding
            (tenant_id, data_source_id, source_device_key_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, from_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, to_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id),
    CHECK (from_asset_id IS DISTINCT FROM to_asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE event_registry (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    event_id uuid NOT NULL,
    original_asset_id uuid,
    accepted_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, event_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, original_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE security_alert (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    alert_id uuid NOT NULL,
    original_asset_id uuid,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, alert_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, original_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE incident_case (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    incident_id uuid NOT NULL,
    original_asset_id uuid,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, incident_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, original_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE forensic_evidence (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    evidence_id uuid NOT NULL,
    content_sha256 bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(content_sha256) = 32),
    immutable_object_ref text NOT NULL,
    captured_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, evidence_id)
);

CREATE TABLE asset_event_lineage (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    event_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    related_asset_id uuid NOT NULL,
    relation text NOT NULL CHECK (
        relation IN ('reassigned_view', 'split_attribution', 'merged_into', 'reviewed')
    ),
    evidence_ref text NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, event_id, operation_id, related_asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, event_id)
        REFERENCES event_registry (tenant_id, event_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, related_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE asset_alert_lineage (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    alert_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    related_asset_id uuid NOT NULL,
    relation text NOT NULL CHECK (
        relation IN ('reassigned_view', 'split_attribution', 'merged_into', 'reviewed')
    ),
    evidence_ref text NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, alert_id, operation_id, related_asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, alert_id)
        REFERENCES security_alert (tenant_id, alert_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, related_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE incident_asset_lineage (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    incident_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    related_asset_id uuid NOT NULL,
    relation text NOT NULL CHECK (
        relation IN ('reassigned_view', 'split_attribution', 'merged_into', 'reviewed')
    ),
    evidence_ref text NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, incident_id, operation_id, related_asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, incident_id)
        REFERENCES incident_case (tenant_id, incident_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, related_asset_id)
        REFERENCES asset (tenant_id, asset_id)
);

CREATE TABLE asset_identity_operation_evidence (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    evidence_id uuid NOT NULL,
    evidence_role text NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, operation_id, evidence_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, evidence_id)
        REFERENCES forensic_evidence (tenant_id, evidence_id)
);

CREATE TABLE tenant_license_usage (
    tenant_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES tenant (tenant_id),
    licensed_quota bigint NOT NULL CHECK (licensed_quota >= 0),
    active_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (active_count >= 0),
    reserved_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (reserved_count >= 0),
    pending_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (pending_count >= 0),
    version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (version >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE asset_license_event (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    license_event_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid,
    idempotency_key text NOT NULL,
    event_kind text NOT NULL,
    active_delta bigint NOT NULL,
    reserved_delta bigint NOT NULL,
    pending_delta bigint NOT NULL,
    before_version bigint NOT NULL,
    after_version bigint NOT NULL,
    actor text NOT NULL,
    reason text NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, license_event_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id),
    CHECK (after_version = before_version + 1)
);

CREATE TABLE identity_operation_outbox (
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    outbox_id uuid NOT NULL,
    operation_id uuid NOT NULL,
    idempotency_key text NOT NULL,
    message_type text NOT NULL,
    payload jsonb NOT NULL,
    state text NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('pending', 'leased', 'delivered', 'retry_wait', 'dead_letter')
    ),
    attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempts >= 0),
    next_attempt_at timestamptz,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, outbox_id),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key),
    FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, operation_id)
        REFERENCES asset_identity_operation (tenant_id, operation_id)
);

Additional constraints/decisions:

  • event_registry is an unpartitioned tenant/event identity ledger. Partitioned event storage must reference it or use an equivalent globally enforceable event identity. PostgreSQL partitioned-table uniqueness often must include partition keys; do not assume a global FK/unique key exists across arbitrary partitions.
  • In a complete schema, operation-item rows for alert and incident references should use separate typed tables with composite (tenant_id, alert_id) and (tenant_id, incident_id) FKs. Do not use an unvalidated polymorphic (object_type, object_id) as the only integrity mechanism.
  • Forensic evidence may be external immutable blobs. Store tenant, immutable evidence ID, content hash, capture time, source, custody/access metadata, and a signed/immutable object reference; do not copy or rewrite original evidence during merge/split.
  • Restrict updates to event_registry.original_asset_id and security_alert.original_asset_id (for example, column-level grants plus a defensive trigger). incident_case.original_asset_id and the evidence hash/reference are likewise immutable after acceptance. Corrected associations go only into lineage tables.
  • The asset_license_event version check is a local example. Serialize updates by locking the tenant usage row and compare the expected version before applying deltas. Verify deltas against owner-approved lifecycle policy.
  • Add asset_identity_operation_evidence referencing a tenant-scoped evidence record in the final schema. evidence_summary_ref is not by itself a substitute for evidence integrity.
  • Runtime roles must not delete or update committed operation, lineage, license ledger, audit, or evidence records. Corrections add new rows and compensating operations.

7.3 Merge/split transaction and outbox behavior

Merge:

  1. Authenticate tenant actor and required privilege; verify evidence and any owner-approved second approver.
  2. Lock tenant licensing row, then both assets in ascending UUID order, then source bindings in stable order.
  3. Recheck exact identity claims, lifecycle states, idempotency, binding ownership, and source/evidence mapping.
  4. Create asset_identity_operation, asset items, explicit binding assignment history, and any event/alert/incident lineage. Update current binding assignments and losing asset to merged tombstone. Do not rewrite original event/alert/evidence records.
  5. Apply one usage decrement only if two licensed canonical assets are verified to represent one device and owner-approved billing semantics permit it. Record the ledger delta.
  6. Insert outbox messages in the same transaction; mark operation committed and idempotency result; commit.

Split:

  1. Require explicit evidence and a complete map of bindings/observations to remain versus move. Ambiguous rows remain quarantined.
  2. Lock tenant usage, source asset, and selected bindings in deterministic order; recheck quota and identity conflict.
  3. Create a new asset UUID, operation items, assignment history, event/alert/incident lineage, and a license increment only if a second unique monitored device is established and quota permits.
  4. Insert outbox messages and commit all database changes atomically.

External side effects: Outbox consumers may retry. Each consumer uses (tenant_id, outbox_id/idempotency_key) and an external idempotency token where supported. If an external provider cannot deduplicate, record request/response references and reconcile before retrying potentially non-idempotent actions. The database operation remains committed even if delivery fails; outbox state moves through retry/dead-letter and alerts operators.

Partial failure: Before PostgreSQL commit, the whole transaction rolls back. After commit, no database rollback can retract an email, ticket update, containment action, export, or external API call. Record the side effect and result; if correction is needed, create a new authorized compensating operation that references the original operation and produces new lineage/license/audit/outbox rows. Never delete or rewrite original evidence, operation, audit, or license history.

7.4 Idempotency and operation state

(tenant_id, idempotency_key) identifies one requested merge/split operation. A retry with the same key returns the stored operation result; the same key with a different normalized request hash is rejected and audited. The transaction's unique constraint is the final guard.

Operation state is prepared only inside a controlled transaction/workflow; committed records the durable change; failed records a terminal rejected/aborted operation only if its audit record can be safely committed separately; cancelled records an authorized cancellation. External outbox delivery state is separate from operation state.

Reversibility boundary: Before commit, PostgreSQL rollback is safe. After commit, a compensating operation is required. A historical operation record does not imply a mechanically reversible action.

8. Threat and failure scenarios

Threat/failure Prevention/detection Recovery
Same-tenant wrong binding ID substituted into rotation item Four-column FK tying identifier record to exact tenant/source/binding Reject insert/update; audit integrity failure
Cross-tenant alias/claim/operation reference Composite tenant FKs plus forced RLS Deny; alert on repeated attempts
Runtime forges app.tenant_id RLS derives tenant from verified signed context, not bare GUC Deny mismatched/invalid assertion; security audit
API accepts user-supplied tenant as authority Membership resolution and context signer are server-side No token minted; no tenant transaction
Two connectors use same weak ID like device-42 Scope identity by authenticated data source and namespace Do not collapse across connectors absent verified cross-source claim
Firewall IP reused by a different device IP never auto-authorizes attach Pending identity or separate verified asset
VM clone copies machine ID/agent credential Duplicate claim conflict and source provenance Quarantine; rotate/re-enroll credentials; human review
Claim key rotated but old alias re-HMACed Versioned alias key and rotation process Reject unsafe derivation; use protected original or re-observation
Worker continues after lease reclaimed Lease token plus expiry checked in apply transaction Stale worker rolls back; new owner processes
Run marked complete while new binding missed Registration dual-write and final full anti-join under policy lock Keep run in verifying/needs_review; backfill missing alias
KMS outage exhausts all item retries Circuit breaker pauses run; bounded retry per item Same run resumes after key/service health verification
Merge transfers bindings but external notification fails Transactional outbox DB state remains committed; retry/dead-letter outbox; compensate if required
Split changes historical event rows Immutable original event attribution; append lineage only Correct using new lineage/compensation, preserve original
Support grant is replayed or used after expiry Short-lived signed scoped token and grant verification Deny; audit; revoke grant/key if compromised
Pool leaks previous tenant scope Transaction-local context, strict rollback/reset, one tenant per transaction Discard suspect connection, alert, run isolation tests
Owner/migration role reachable from runtime Role separation, NOLOGIN owner, no membership/BYPASSRLS Revoke grants, investigate, rotate credentials

10. Unresolved owner decisions

These remain open; this review does not choose on the owner's behalf:

  1. Which source types may retain recoverable identifiers, for what purpose, and for what retention period.
  2. KMS provider, tenant/key scope, key custodians, rotation authorization, emergency revocation, and backup/recovery policy.
  3. Source-specific normalization and authoritative identity catalogs; which exact provider/vendor identifiers are exclusive and trustworthy enough for automatic attachment.
  4. What evidence is sufficient for customer/operator-confirmed identity mapping; merge/split authorization and second-person approval.
  5. Policy for cloned agents/VMs, duplicate enrollment credentials, and replacement-device workflows.
  6. Pending identity payload retention/quarantine duration and whether pending cases reserve quota.
  7. 30-day reactivation grace, deactivated quota reservation, reserved billing, immediate release exceptions, and permanent-removal authority.
  8. Retention for claim aliases, event/alert/incident lineage, audit, evidence, and backups.
  9. Whether the tenant-context verifier will use PostgreSQL pgcrypto HMAC verification or another reviewed verifier, and how its key is custodied/rotated.
  10. JIT support grant approver roles, maximum duration, allowed scopes, and break-glass process.
  11. Automatic retry limits/backoff values and which item failures block run completion.
  12. Which source types are asset-birth-authorized and must provide a cross-source identity path; whether observation-only sources (such as firewall telemetry or scanners without inventory mapping) always remain pending until mapped.

12. Recommended acceptance tests

All tests below must use PostgreSQL and production-equivalent roles. They are requirements for future testing, not tests run by this documentation task.

Relational integrity

  1. Attempt to reference a source identifier record from another binding in the same tenant: composite FK rejects it.
  2. Attempt to reference an identifier record from another tenant: FK/RLS rejects it.
  3. Attempt to insert an alias referencing another data source or tenant binding: FK rejects it.
  4. Verify one data source can bind many device keys and multiple data sources can bind to one asset.
  5. Verify the same exact (tenant, source, fingerprint_key_id, digest) cannot point to two bindings.
  6. Verify old/new fingerprint versions coexist and both resolve to the same stable source key/asset.
  7. Verify key policy cannot activate two keys or change policy without the prescribed lock/procedure.
  8. Verify pending binding has no asset and cannot enter normal asset-attributed ingestion.

Rotation and recovery

  1. Kill a worker after lease commit; reclaim expired lease and confirm stale lease token cannot apply.
  2. Kill worker before and after the alias/item transaction; verify either both alias and completion commit or neither does.
  3. Simulate commit success/client timeout; retry reads committed outcome without duplicate alias.
  4. Run two workers concurrently on the same batch and verify exactly-once committed alias/item state.
  5. Inject transient database and KMS errors; verify capped exponential retry/jitter and pause circuit behavior.
  6. Exercise permanent AEAD failure, alias collision, authorization failure, and revoked old HMAC key; verify conflict/failure path and no new asset/quota.
  7. Resume a paused run and verify same run ID/history; verify terminal failed run cannot resume and retry requires a linked new run.
  8. Create new bindings during rotation; final anti-join finds no missing aliases or refuses completion.
  9. Change identifier secret during KMS preparation; stale digest is rejected and recalculated.

Cross-source identity

  1. Linux Agent and firewall report one server: only authoritative/reviewed mapping yields one asset; IP/hostname-only input stays pending.
  2. Two scanners report one device using different target IDs: verified mapping attaches both bindings without usage increase.
  3. Change IP and hostname; canonical asset and license count remain stable.
  4. Reuse an IP for a different endpoint; no automatic attachment/merge occurs.
  5. Clone a VM/agent identity; duplicate authoritative claim creates conflict and does not merge or double-bill.
  6. Replace a device at the same IP/hostname; explicit replacement path creates correct distinct identity; old evidence remains.
  7. Submit contradictory serial/MAC/provider claims; automatic merge is blocked and human review is recorded.
  8. Confirm numeric confidence score alone cannot trigger attach/merge.

Tenant isolation

  1. Run all Section 6.7 negative cases with runtime and worker roles; verify default deny, RLS USING/WITH CHECK, and no BYPASSRLS.
  2. Verify signed context rejects forged, expired, wrong-tenant, wrong-scope, wrong-audience, and replayed cross-tenant assertions.
  3. Verify pool reuse and cancellation do not leak context; test concurrent tenants.
  4. Verify runtime cannot assume owner/migrator roles, alter RLS, disable policies, or read verifier keys.
  5. Verify support JIT access expires/revokes and records sensitive reads.

Merge/split and lineage

  1. Retry identical operation ID/idempotency key after timeout; same result and no duplicate count/lineage/outbox rows.
  2. Reuse idempotency key with a different request hash; reject and audit.
  3. Inject failures at each write before commit; all operation, binding, lineage, license, and outbox changes roll back together.
  4. Deliver outbox messages at least twice; consumer idempotency prevents duplicate external actions where supported.
  5. Simulate external delivery failure after DB commit; operation remains committed, outbox retries/dead-letters, no false rollback status.
  6. Merge two verified duplicates; preserve original event/alert/evidence attribution, record source binding moves, and apply one approved usage decrement.
  7. Split one asset into two verified devices; require quota, preserve original attribution, and add lineage plus one approved usage increment.
  8. Perform compensation; original operation/evidence/ledger remain immutable and new compensating history is appended.
  9. Test partitioned event storage and event_registry FK/uniqueness behavior across partition boundaries.

14. Final status

  • EXISTING APPROVED REQUIREMENT: CARES platform constraints and original ten-phase roadmap are preserved.
  • NEW TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: Composite identifier-record FK, durable retry state machines, evidence-based cross-source resolution, verified tenant context under RLS, and immutable operation/event lineage.
  • OWNER DECISION REQUIRED: Source identity authorities, encryption/key custody, lifecycle/billing, pending quarantine, retry policy approval, signed-context verifier implementation, and support/JIT policy remain open.
  • NOT IMPLEMENTED: The DDL, RLS, tenant context, identity resolver, rotation, licensing, operation/outbox, and merge/split designs are not implemented.
  • NOT TESTED: No PostgreSQL integration, concurrency, tenant-isolation, recovery, or lineage tests have been run.
  • Readiness: Ready for formal PostgreSQL schema/security review; not ready for production migrations or implementation.
